format: Each front end of the engine (architecture/engine.md, Parity), and the manifest it published at a pinned commit, as a file in checks/front-ends/: the CLI's is `weblisk commands --json`, Studio's is GET /api/operations, both the engine's one manifest (ops.Catalogue) at the engine the commit builds against. `executors` holds the --parity leg to the operations of those executors in the catalogue and in each manifest: S1 is done for local and tenant-api (ENGINE_PLAN, Order). `expected_gaps` is what the leg finds, measured, and is held exactly: a gap that closes leaves the list, a new one fails. Every gap today is the engine's (today's spellings, and builds and changes still cli-in-tenant), so each closes in the engine (E2 to E4, T1), not in a front end. A front end with no manifest makes checks/front-end-parity.py --parity NOT RUN, never ok.
